text:
Josh: Quick follow-up from the offload RFC — proposal sketch for a "soft-residency" signal plus per-request urgency hints so callers can express tolerance for eviction. Want to sync API shape + fallback semantics before I open the PR.

Amy: this sounds useful. can you outline the priority levels? also how does billing interact if we pin vs allow-evict? :thinking:

Josh: idea: three urgency tiers — prefer-resident, opportunistic, recompute-friendly.
- prefer-resident: allocator should avoid eviction unless hard OOM, may trigger reserved staging pool.
- opportunistic: allocator can evict normal resident pages for higher throughput, try to rehydrate from host or storage.
- recompute-friendly: prefer recompute over fetch when recompute cost < fetch latency/cost.

Nate: interesting. how do we convey recompute cost? we need a cost model exposed from runtime to the eviction planner. maybe a simple numeric hint: recompute_cost_ms or compute_cycles_estimate?

Amy: +1 for a numeric estimate, but worried about gamable values from callers. we should default to conservative heuristics if the header is missing or outside sane bounds.

Josh: agreed. plan: request header prototype:

```
X-Redwood-Residency: prefer-resident; urgency=prefer-resident; recompute_cost_ms=25
```

Or in the SDK call options: { residency: "prefer-resident", recompute_cost_ms: 25 }

Sara: SLA/billing question — if a customer pins resident and we reserve a staging slot, do we charge reserved capacity vs standard tokens? we need clear user-facing semantics. Also security: pinned pages for private deployments need KMS considerations.

Josh: billing note: prefer-resident should map to capacity reservation if the customer has Dedicated or Private. For Hosted, it should default to best-effort unless they buy reserved capacity add-on. We'll add a clear error/response header if reservation couldn't be honored.

Nate: implementation concerns: allocator needs a quick path to mark pages as soft-protected and a background reclaimer that respects urgency and recompute_cost_ms. We can piggyback on existing lease tokens but add an urgency bit. Evictor scoring function to include:
score = base_eviction_score - urgency_weight * urgency_hint + recompute_penalty(recompute_cost_ms)

Josh: here's a tiny pseudo-config for the evictor:

```
evictor:
  urgency_weights:
    prefer-resident: 50
    opportunistic: 10
    recompute-friendly: -20
  recompute_cost_scale_ms: 1.5
  host_fetch_latency_ms: 75
```

Amy: small UX ask: runtime should surface a metric like resident_hit_ratio_by_urgency and average_rehydrate_latency_by_model so customers can tune their flags.

runtime-bot: telemetry: created chart "residency.resident_hit_ratio_by_urgency" linked -> https://console.internal/telemetry/residency/7423456789 :white_check_mark:

Sara: edge case: multi-tenant noisy neighbor — if one tenant sets prefer-resident happily, we can't let them starve others. need admission control and a per-tenant resident_quota. That ties back to Dedicated reserved pools or a fairness scoring tweak.

Nate: also consider cross-node rehydration vs recompute. if host fetch involves RPC across racks it's often worse than recompute. the runtime should consider topology (local host, same-pool, remote-pool) in the cost model.

Josh: agree. topology-aware rehydrate cost will be part of the planner. Implementation timeline suggestion:
1) API + header sketch (this week)
2) evictor scoring + telemetry prototype (next sprint)
3) RFC + tests + SDK support (in two sprints)

Amy: Sounds good. please include default server-side caps so callers can't abuse recompute_cost_ms. Also add a validation warning in SDK if value looks unrealistic.

Josh: action items: I'll open the RFC PR with the header shape, scoring pseudo-code, and a short benchmark comparing recompute vs host-fetch for our common models. tagging @Amy and @Nate for review.

Sara: can you also add a note about billing/Reserved semantics so product knows what to surface?

Josh: will do. thanks all.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: pinned-telemetry:residency-hook v0.3 deployed to staging at 7423456805

Nate: small addendum — we should also consider a fallback policy enum in responses: fallback=rehydrate|recompute|degraded-output so caller apps can adapt.

Josh: good call. I'll include that in the RFC and a couple of example SDK behaviors (retry vs degrade).
